picks.title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
picks.excerpt: Amazon-owned Bee has launched its first new AI devices since its acquisition, including an updated wearable and a credit-card-sized recorder that attaches to smartphones. The devices can summarize conversations, create to-do lists, and integrate with Alexa and Amazon shopping, with prices starting a
picks.rationale: Bee ships its first post-acquisition hardware (an updated wearable and a card-sized phone-mounted recorder from $75), tied to Alexa, shopping and a new Bee Pro subscription. It is a new product launch.

picks.title: Meta and Apple Bring Muse Spark Open AI Model to Mac Studio
picks.excerpt: Meta today announced the release of Muse Spark Open, which it says is the "most capable U.S. open-weight model to date". Meta worked with Apple to bring Muse Spark Open to the Mac, and the model can run on a desktop setup with two 512GB Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios running the latest MLX framework. Me
picks.rationale: Meta releases an open-weight Muse Spark model and, with Apple, makes it run locally on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX. This is a new model release with a concrete desk-side hardware recipe.

picks.title: Sipeed reveals Chinese-made DGX Spark and Ryzen AI Halo rival, expected to cost $3,999
picks.excerpt: Sipeed’s MaixStation pairs Axera’s AX8860P with 128GB of LPDDR5X at 273 GB/s to take on Nvidia’s DGX Spark and AMD’s Ryzen AI Halo.
picks.rationale: Sipeed unveils MaixStation, a $3,999 local-AI box built on a Chinese Axera chip with 128GB of memory. It is a new non-Nvidia, non-AMD option for desk-side AI.

picks.title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
picks.excerpt: Eiliko and its manufacturer, Energize Lab, are seemingly not to be trusted.
picks.rationale: A Verge investigation found that the Eiliko AI companion robot sends user conversations to poorly secured servers. It is a new, concrete privacy finding about a consumer AI device.

picks.title: A $7 board lets an AI control an iPhone without jailbreaking it
picks.excerpt: Henry Yuan’s open-source project uses a roughly $7 board to let AI navigate an iPhone without jailbreaking it, though model access and setup requirements make it more involved than the price suggests.
picks.rationale: An open-source project uses a cheap microcontroller acting as a keyboard and mouse so an AI agent can drive a stock iPhone. That gives a hands-on way to test agent-driven phone UI flows.

alternates.title: Nothing reportedly launching two pairs of smart glasses, one with barely any AI
alternates.excerpt: A reliable source says that Nothing is building out its own AI smart glasses that feature ChatGPT integration, a camera,...
alternates.rationale: This is a report or leak, not a launch, and it was already an alternate yesterday. It is an alternate again.

alternates.title: Gemini for Home is finally learning that ‘stop’ means stop
alternates.excerpt: Google Home's October update teaches Gemini for Home to reliably obey 'stop' and other voice commands on speakers and displays.
alternates.rationale: The October update is a new release, separate from the 10-02 September update card, but it is an incremental fix.

alternates.title: AI agents are coming to Rivian’s cars
alternates.excerpt: We'll likely learn more about how this will work at the company's upcoming "AI & Autonomy Day" event in December.
alternates.rationale: This is a new announcement, but the details are deferred to a December event. It is an alternate.

Tom's Guide RTX Spark benchmarks and Tom's Hardware Surface Laptop Ultra RTX Spark test are reviews of the platform already covered 10-08 (TechCrunch Microsoft Nvidia-chip AI PCs) and 10-10 (TechRadar RTX Spark pre-orders), with no new release. Ars 'Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware' (10-08) repeats the 10-08 TechCrunch/Verge cards. Engadget Alexa Tablet 12 Pro review repeats the 10-09 Engadget Alexa tablets launch. MacRumors 'Which Apple Home devices get Siri AI' and CNET HomePod mini 2 hands-on are coverage of the Oct 13 Apple event already published 10-14 (Ars HomeView). 9to5Google 'Meta fixed Ray-Ban recording issue' is a follow-up to the 10-14 Android Authority Ray-Ban listening card; it was not kept. Lower priority: Panos Panay Disrupt interview (commentary, and it overlaps the Bee pick), Samsung Galaxy AI language expansion (incremental), MacPaw Eney, etnews AimFuture chip and robot guard dog. Alternates: Nothing glasses report, Gemini for Home October update and Rivian AI agents. The final 5 come from 5 distinct outlets (TechCrunch, MacRumors, Tom's Hardware, The Verge, Digital Trends) and cover a wearable, an open-weight model on a Mac, local-AI hardware, AI toy privacy and phone agent control.
